title: Shifted localization models are orthogonal to localized modules
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, with ordinary derived category $D(A)$ on the one-object bottom site [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of $A$, and let $(T,\epsilon_T)$ satisfy the ordered localization model predicate [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-cech-data] for $I$. Let $s\in I$ and let $M$ be an $A$-module sheaf on that site such that multiplication by $s$ on its value at the unique object is bijective. For every integer $n$ and every object $X$ isomorphic to $Q(T)[n]$, every morphism $X\to Q(M[0])$ is zero. Here $M[0]$ denotes the single complex in degree zero. No target Cech model, K-flatness or map of rings is assumed.

proof.text: Apply ringComplex_cech_cohomology_power_torsion to the given model and s in I. This supplies an annihilating power of s for every cohomology class of T, without mentioning the target module.

Unpack membership of X in the shift closure of the singleton Q(T): there is an isomorphism e:X -> Q(T)[n]. Apply power_torsion_localized_shift_hom to e.inv followed by the given map into Q(M[0]). It is zero. Compose with e.hom and use the inverse equation to recover that the original map is zero.

theorem ringComplex_cech_localized_orthogonality
    (A : CommRingCat.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (RingSiteModules A)]
    (I : {I : Ideal A // I.FG})
    (T : CochainComplex (RingSiteModules A) ℤ) (εT : T ⟶ ringComplexSingle A)
    (hT : RingComplexHasCechModel A I.val T εT)
    (s : A) (hs : s ∈ I.val) (M : RingSiteModules A)
    (hM : Function.Bijective
      (fun x : M.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) ↦ s • x)) :
    ((ObjectProperty.singleton (DerivedCategory.Q.obj T)).shiftClosure ℤ).rightOrthogonal
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((HomologicalComplex.single (RingSiteModules A) (.up ℤ) 0).obj M))
